# Uzbekistan FIFA World Cup 2026 preview: Cannavaro’s White Wolves aim to make a splash
[...]
Uzbekistan has already created history by qualifying for the World Cup for the first time ever. The side excelled in the second and third rounds of AFC qualifying, losing just a solitary game, to book its tickets to the World Cup.
[...]
Despite Timur Kapadze leading the team into its maiden World Cup, the White Wolves have opted to go a different route to wade through the pressure of the tournament, appointing Fabio Cannavaro as the head coach in 2025. The 2006 World Cup-winning captain will hope he can transfer his experience of the big stage onto the youthful Uzbek group who will have no fear of failure.
[...]
Uzbekistan deploys a three-man central defence and is a team built on solidity and physical presence. The player and the manager pride themselves on being difficult to break down and the Central Asian nation will look to be thorn in the side of the bigger teams in the group.
[...]
Player to watch out for
[...]
Abdukodir Khusanov: The 22-year-old defender has had a breakout year in Manchester City blue, deputising admirably well for the injured Ruben Dias. He has already accumulated 25 caps for his nation and will look to be a leader on the pitch in its first World Cup appearance.
[...]
Not many managers at this World Cup can boast about being Ballon d’Or winners. In fact Cannavaro is the only one who can stake a claim. The Italian legend started his coaching career in the top Asian leagues and took over Uzbekistan after a brief 14-game stay at Dinamo Zagreb of Croatia where it beat his old nemesis AC Milan in the group stage.
[...]

The question for bettors is not whether Uzbekistan win the whole thing — the odds on that make it a novelty play at best — but whether there is any exploitable value in the secondary markets, where the gap between expectation and price can be narrower.

Uzbekistan World Cup 2026 Preview: Odds, Picks, Players to Watch & Predictions
[...]
Uzbekistan will make their first ever World Cup appearance as an independent nation this summer, having made it through the AFC qualifying campaign. Uzbekistan are one of the biggest underdogs in the competition this summer, and they have been drawn in Group K alongside Portugal, Colombia and DR Congo.
[...]
## ✅ What is the best bet for Uzbekistan at the World Cup 2026?
[...]
Group K is a difficult draw for a nation making their World Cup debut, so Uzbekistan look set to struggle. Portugal are one of the favourites in the competition, and they need no introduction, while Colombia are another side with plenty of elite talent playing across Europe’s top leagues. DR Congo are also not a side to underestimate, and they recently made it out of their AFCON group, before falling to Algeria only after extra time in the first knockout round.
[...]
Uzbekistan's route to their first World Cup was surprisingly comfortable - they finished 2nd in their group to secure automatic qualification to the World Cup alongside Iran, bypassing any further play-off rounds. Uzbekistan were six points clear of the UAE, and eight points above Qatar, which was a significant gap, and they only lost one of their 10 matches in total.
[...]
